row.notes: mov r8,rax (3 bytes) in Game_CareerEventsSequencer_Initialise (+0x1037), right after the call to Ent_Get_Driver_Thunk (0x1423dbcf0 at 0x140c72eaa, rcx = r13 = the entrants system, rdx = the first collected team record + 0x50 = its packed driver ref: domain byte +0x50, u16 stat id +0x52). rax is the team mate's driver record, or 0 when the ref names no driver (domain above 2, no driver table for the domain, id past the table's end, or an empty slot). The next instruction calls Game_CareerEventResourceManager_AddDriverMorphData (0x140c808e0, rcx = [rsp+0x38], rdx = r13, r8 = rax), which reads [r8+8] at +0x82 (0x140c80962) with no test and faults reading 0x8 when the team mate's driver is not in the entrants system (crash reports reading 0x8 at Game_CareerEventResourceManager_AddDriverMorphData+0x82 from Initialise+0x103f as a My Team or Progressive career session is entered). Core hooks it and, for rax == 0, sets rip to site_Game_CareerEventsSequencerTeamMateDriverJoin. A 5-byte jump covers this instruction and the call (relocated); a 14-byte jump would be refused for the call's rel32, so the join is never inside the patch.
